What is personal (ratione personae) immunity?

A. Personal immunity is afforded to all physical persons

question:
Which proposition below may be characterized as the most powerful refutation by Hart of Lord Devlin's argument?

A. Society has no right to preserve its moral and social cohesion through the criminal law.

question: I work in a shop where a majority of coworkers signed union authorization cards, but management refuses to recognize the union, insists on an NLRB election, and immediately started subcontracting core jobs to non-union contractors while cutting hours and threatening discipline for “union activity.” Can I compel the employer to recognize and bargain with the union and stop the subcontracting and retaliation as unfair labor practices under the NLRA, or am I required to go through an election first?
gold_response: Under the NLRA, a clear majority showing can justify employer recognition and a duty to bargain, but the employer may lawfully demand an NLRB election unless its refusal is motivated by unfair labor practices that undermine a fair election. Immediate subcontracting of core unit work, cutting hours, and threats or discipline for “union activity” are classic unfair labor practices (Sections 8(a)(1) and 8(a)(3)/(1)) and can independently require remedial relief. If those actions were taken to frustrate majority support or to coerce employees, you should file an unfair labor practice charge with the NLRB; the Board can order bargaining or block an election and, in egregious cases, issue a Gissel bargaining order or seek Section 10(j) injunctive relief in federal court. Outcome depends on facts (how clear the majority is, timing, motive for subcontracting, unit scope) and Board precedent. So you are not automatically stuck with an election first: file a ULP charge promptly, document evidence, and the NLRB will decide whether to require recognition, enjoin the subcontracting/retaliation, or direct an election.
